title: Quintessential Bitter American French Lentils Skillet
description: A hearty, bitter, and chewy American dish featuring French lentils, perfect for a weeknight dinner, this macrobiotic-friendly recipe is cooked to perfection in a cast-iron skillet.
instructions: Rinse the French lentils and pick out any debris or stones.
In a cast-iron skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the French lentils, water, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper to the skillet, stirring to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
While the lentils are cooking, massage the chopped kale with your hands for about 2 minutes to help break down the cell walls and make it more tender.
After the lentils have cooked for 30 minutes, stir in the massaged kale and continue to simmer, covered, for an additional 10 minutes, or until the kale is wilted.
Stir in the apple cider vinegar and cook for an additional minute.
Serve the Quintessential Bitter American French Lentils Skillet hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
